subject: Renewal pulse check: rebalancing GPU pool + SKU credit mechanics
messages:
From: Sofia Bianchi <sofia@brightarc.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco@brightarc.ai>, procurement@brightarc.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Quick check ahead of renewal — possible mid-term rebalancing?

Hi Chloe,

Hope you’re well — we’re starting internal planning for our Q1 workloads and want to check a couple of things ahead of the renewal call. Our usage patterns shifted after the last compute-heavy release: short spikes in inference require higher peak concurrency but average token throughput is down ~12%.

Two asks:
- Is there a straightforward path to shift committed vGPU units from a flat pool to a banded profile (baseline + burst) mid-term? We like the predictability of a reserved commit but want more headroom for bursts without paying full-time for it.
- If we move ~40 GPUs of our 180-GPU commit into a burst/elastic tranche, how would that affect the effective per-token rate and any step-down discounts at renewal?

We’ll need the details for procurement (budget signoff + internal playbook). Attaching the updated mutual action plan with usage slices.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Bianchi
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightArc AI

Attachment: BrightArc_MAPlan_v3.xlsx (attachment)
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Bianchi <sofia@brightarc.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick check ahead of renewal — possible mid-term rebalancing?

Thanks Sofia — appreciate the heads-up and the plan. Short answers up front: yes, and yes — with caveats.

Overview:
- Mid-term rebalance: We can reclassify GPUs inside a committed pool into a baseline (reserved) band and a burst/elastic band. This is an amendment to the Dedicated contract (midterm uplift/reprofile).
- Economics: Moving GPUs to burst typically increases the per-GPU effective unit price for the burst tranche, but we can preserve most of your overall blended rate via a transitional credit ("rebalance credit") tied to remaining term and usage.

What I’ll do next:
1) Karthik will provide the pricing math (per-band rate, blended impact, and any minimum throughput SLO changes).
2) I’ll draft a short amendment showing the pool split, credits, and an SLA table comparing baseline vs burst throughput guarantees.
3) Marissa will outline discount options if you are also increasing the committed baseline at renewal.

Can you confirm the exact 40 GPUs you referenced are currently pooled under commit SKU: DED-180-v2? If yes, we’ll model two scenarios: (A) convert 40 GPUs to burst for the remaining 7 months; (B) convert now + top up baseline by 20 GPUs at renewal.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Bianchi <sofia@brightarc.ai>, chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick check ahead of renewal — pricing mechanics and throughput SLOs

Sofia — following Chloe’s note, sketched numbers below. I attached a small matrix (SLA_Diff_Matrix.pdf) describing baseline vs burst expectations.

Assumptions: current commit DED-180-v2, remaining term = 7 months, blended effective unit price today = $0.95/GPU-hour equivalent for committed baseline.

Scenario A (reclass 40 -> burst, no renewal top-up):
- Baseline becomes 140 GPUs at $0.97/GPU-hr (minor uplift to reflect smaller baseline pool).
- Burst tranche 40 GPUs billed at $1.45/GPU-hr when used; unutilized burst capacity billed at 20% of full for reservation buffering.
- Rebalance credit: a one-time credit equal to 60% of the delta between legacy blended spend and modeled spend over remaining term. This keeps your net spend within ~5% of current run-rate.

Scenario B (reclass 40 -> burst now, commit +20 at renewal):
- Renewal commit becomes 160 baseline + 40 burst; renewing baseline rate eligible for stepped discount (3% additional discount at renewal for a 20+ GPU increase).
- We can offer an incremental renewal credit (tiered) that phases out over 12 months so BrightArc doesn’t see a sudden jump.

SLO notes: baseline retains 99.9% throughput window for median p50 latency SLAs; burst does not carry the same latency guarantees (best-effort, with priority ramping). We’ll provide a migration runbook to preserve inference KV cache behavior during rebalances.

Next steps: Chloe — can you confirm which scenario Sofia prefers? I’ll prepare the line-item tradeoffs and a blended quote.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions & Pricing | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sofia Bianchi <sofia@brightarc.ai>, chloe_martin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T10:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick check ahead of renewal — rebalancing proposal and discount pathways

Sofia — quick note from the commercial side. We want to keep the path to your preferred outcome as simple as possible. Two commercial levers we can pull:

1) One-time rebalance credit (what Karthik outlined) to smooth your remaining term — available for scenario A. Typical credit range we’re comfortable with: 45–65% of modeled delta depending on historical utilization.

2) Renewal uplift incentive — if you commit to >= +20 baseline GPUs at renewal we can add a 3–6% incremental discount on the renewed baseline band plus 2 months of complimentary burst buffer (no charge) to ease the transition. This is approval-dependent; I can escalate a formal approval route if you want guarantees in writing.

If procurement needs a short finance-friendly line (to include in your budget packet) I can provide the blended spend comparison (current vs post-rebalance) and a one-page rationale for the credit.

If you confirm scenario B (top-up at renewal), flag here and I’ll start the approval packet for a 4% incremental discount and 60-day free burst buffer (subject to legal sign-off).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals & Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Cc: procurement@brightarc.ai, Marco Ruiz <marco@brightarc.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T15:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick check ahead of renewal — rebalancing proposal and discount pathways

Thanks all — this is helpful and aligns with what our finance team wants to see. We’re leaning toward scenario B: reclass 40 GPUs to burst now to handle immediate spikes, and increase baseline by 20 GPUs at renewal. Procurement asked for two items before we proceed:

1) A concise blended spend comparison (current vs scenario B) — one table, one chart, suitable for CFO review.
2) The proposed amendment wording for the mid-term reprofile (simple language on how credits are calculated and the expected dates for the burst tranche to be active).

If you can get those over by EOD Friday our procurement lead will slot it for review next week. Also — the renewal window closes on 2027-01-15, we can align incentives to that date.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Sofia
Sofia Bianchi
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightArc AI
